title: SCIM: bulk reconciliation, backfill & admin restore workflow for deprovisioned users
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a safe, observable bulk reconciliation and backfill pipeline for SCIM provisioning that handles large orgs and transient IdP inconsistencies. The feature should: (1) detect drift between IdP and Redwood user/group state, (2) perform idempotent upserts for users and groups with retry/jitter and circuit-breaker protections, (3) soft-deprovision and surface recoverability via an admin restore workflow, and (4) emit audit events compatible with RBAC v2 and our audit logging schema.
motivation: Multiple customers experience silent drift after large group syncs or missed SCIM webhooks. We need a robust background reconciliation that minimizes false deprovisions, provides an admin-safe restore path, and produces clear audit trails for compliance teams.
design_summary: Implement a batched reconciliation job that reads IdP data (SCIM bulk endpoints or SCIM list responses) and reconciles in phases: validate -> create/update -> group-membership reconcile -> mark-or-queue-deprovision. Use idempotent SCIM upserts keyed by externalId and email, maintain a tombstone layer for 30 days for soft-deleted accounts, and provide an admin UI + API to inspect and restore soft-deleted entries. Integrate exponential backoff with per-org circuit breaker to avoid thrash when IdP is flaky. All reconciliation actions must write structured audit events to the audit log stream with mapping to RBAC v2 roles.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation job can process a 50k-user IdP export for a single org within SLA (24hrs) without OOM or database deadlocks
Upserts are idempotent: retrying the same delta does not create duplicates or clobber identity mappings
Soft-deprovisioned users are retained for configurable retention (default 30 days) and can be restored by a privileged admin via Console and API
All create/update/delete/restore actions emit audit events conforming to audit-schema-v2 and include externalId, actor, timestamp, and reason
Circuit breaker prevents continuous retries against an IdP when failure rate >50% for 10m and reports actionable metrics to SRE
E2E tests that simulate webhook misses, duplicate events, and eventual IdP consistency pass in CI
implementation_steps: Define SCIM reconciliation pipeline contract + idempotency keys (externalId,email) in design doc (Confluence)
Prototype batched upsert worker using existing job-runner and implement per-org rate and concurrency limits
Add tombstone table and soft-delete/restore API + Console surface (design + frontend PR)
Wire audit events in pipeline to audit-producer with RBAC v2 context (role mapping and org_id)
Implement circuit breaker + backoff with randomized jitter and throttling by org
Add monitoring dashboards and alerts (failure-rate, queue-depth, circuit-breaker trips, avg reconciliation latency)
Create e2e test harness to replay IdP exports and webhook gaps and include in CI
notes: We intentionally avoid immediate hard-deprovision on reconciliation runs; deprovisioning requires a separate scheduled purge job post-retention.
Trade-offs: keeping soft-deletes increases storage and access-control complexity but is necessary for enterprise compliance and reduces customer support tickets.
Consider incremental reconciliation (delta-first) for large orgs to reduce load; full exports supported as fallback.
Plan to leverage existing KV cache to accelerate group membership lookups during reconciliation to avoid N+1 DB queries.
qa_plan: Unit tests for idempotent upsert logic and tombstone state machine
Integration tests for group membership reconciliation using synthetic IdP exports
Chaos tests to simulate flaky IdP endpoints and webhook duplication; assert circuit breaker behavior
Manual verification steps for restore: create test user, soft-delete via reconcile, restore via Console, verify tokens invalidated and reissued
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the reconciliation pipeline per-org; start with internal org and opt-in customers
Monitor metrics for 48h with SLO thresholds; enable auto-rollback of pipeline for orgs with >5% unexpected deprovision rate
Gradually enable for enterprise customers based on size and readiness checklist
rollback_plan: Disable reconciliation job for affected orgs and re-run idempotent recovery job from snapshot
If DB schema changes cause issues, revert migrations and rehydrate from backup
Inform customers and SRE via incident channel with remediation steps
security_considerations: Ensure all SCIM HTTP traffic between Redwood and IdP uses mTLS where available; fall back to signed requests
Audit events must not include sensitive tokens or PII beyond allowed fields (externalId, email hashed when required by customer policy)
Admin restore API requires RBAC v2 grant and MFA for console actions; record actor details in audit log
